note: Runtime probes: what the real executor does, asserted mechanically. Run by gate.py --full and out/_release.py; skipped when no JRE or the versioned jars are missing.

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false wet @unit 20
end
probes.why: a bare known status name is applied: LParser normalises it to the @status-wet constant

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false @status-wet @unit 20
end
probes.why: the canonical v160 spelling @status-<name> is applied as well

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false @wet @unit 20
end
probes.why: @<name> is not a status constant: the effect resolves to null and the instruction is a silent no-op

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false status-wet @unit 20
end
probes.why: status-<name> without the at-sign is not a constant either

probes.code:
set s @status-unmoving
ubind @flare
status false s @unit 20
end
probes.why: the effect slot reads a variable: v160's ApplyEffectI takes an LVar, so a variable holding the constant works

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false wet @unit 20
end
probes.why: v159 looks the effect up by exact name, so the bare name is the only spelling that works there

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false @status-wet @unit 20
end
probes.why: the @status- prefix does not exist before v160: the jar's constant pool has no status- literal at all

probes.code:
ubind @flare
status false wet @unit 20
status true wet @unit 0
end
probes.why: unapply() drops the timer but not the applied bit, so hasEffect stays true: read getDuration, never hasEffect

probes.code:
set r 0
op acos r 0.5
end
probes.why: op acos returns DEGREES: Math.acos(0.5) * doubleRadDeg = 60 (float noise 60.00000000000001)

probes.code:
set k 5
localeprint k
end
probes.why: localeprint only appends when the operand is an object: a numeric variable writes nothing

probes.code:
localeprint "no-such-locale-key"
end
probes.why: an unknown map locale key prints the wrapped key (v160.7 jar); the newer source snapshot appends null instead - the jar wins

probes.code:
clientdata "ch" 5 1
end
probes.why: ClientDataStatement.build returns null unless state.rules.allowLogicData: the line compiles to nothing (not even a noop)

probes.code:
clientdata "ch" 5 1
end
probes.why: with the map rule allowLogicData the same line compiles to ClientDataI - the gate is a rule, not a version

probes.code:
ubind @flare
radar enemy any any distance 0 1 u
end
probes.why: radar has exactly one output LVar: the executor writes one unit to it (LExecutor.java:802 output.setobj(targeted)) and there is no loop over a count

probes.code:
ubind @flare
radar enemy any any distance 0 5 u
end
probes.why: the 6th operand is the sort direction: writing 5 lands as the constant ___5.0 in sortOrder and is read as a boolean (LExecutor.java:753), it does not mean 'find 5 units'

probes.code:
ubind @flare
uradar enemy any any distance 1 target
end
probes.why: the 6-operand shape the old doc showed is off by one: 'target' is read as the direction and the result falls through to the default `result` variable

probes.code:
ubind @flare
sensor ctrl @unit @controller
sensor dd @unit @dead
set ok 0
jump 9 equal dd 1
jump 8 equal ctrl @unit
jump 8 equal ctrl @this
jump 9 always
set ok 1
print ok
end
probes.why: an AI unit nobody controls: @controller is the unit itself (UnitComp.java:319) and @dead is 0, so the guard says legal

probes.code:
ubind @flare
sensor ctrl @unit @controller
sensor dd @unit @dead
set ok 0
jump 9 equal dd 1
jump 8 equal ctrl @unit
jump 8 equal ctrl @this
jump 9 always
set ok 1
print ok
end
probes.setup_js: var G = Packages.mindustry.gen.Groups.unit; var U = null; for(var i = 0; i < G.size(); i++){ var q = G.index(i); if(q.team == team){ U = q; break; } } U.kill();
probes.why: @dead is the only check that sees a dead unit: @unit goes stale, and a null @unit also reads @dead = 1 (LExecutor.java:685-688)

probes.code:
ubind @flare
sensor ctrl @unit @controller
sensor dd @unit @dead
set ok 0
jump 9 equal dd 1
jump 8 equal ctrl @unit
jump 8 equal ctrl @this
jump 9 always
set ok 1
print ok
end
probes.why: a unit this processor drives: @controller returns the controlling building, which is @this, so the guard says legal

probes.code:
ubind @flare
sensor ctrl @unit @controller
sensor dd @unit @dead
set ok 0
jump 9 equal dd 1
jump 8 equal ctrl @unit
jump 8 equal ctrl @this
jump 9 always
set ok 1
print ok
end
probes.why: a unit another processor drives: @controller is that building, neither @unit nor @this, so the guard says illegal -- and a later ucontrol would silently steal it (LExecutor.java:324-326)

probes.code:
ubind @flare
ucontrol move 60 60 0 0 0
wait 6
sensor c @unit @controlled
print c
end
probes.why: a unit handed to logic stays controlled while the 600-tick lease runs: wait 6 s = 360 ticks is still inside it

probes.code:
ubind @flare
ucontrol move 60 60 0 0 0
wait 11
sensor c @unit @controlled
print c
end
probes.why: 600 ticks after the last ucontrol the lease expires and the unit reverts: LogicAI.java:59-64 resetController(); every ucontrol re-arms it (LExecutor.java:351)

probes.code:
ubind @fortress
sensor r @unit @range
sensor hp @unit @health
print r
end
probes.why: sensor @unit @range returns the unit type's range (fortress 29.5) and @health its 900 hp

probes.code:
control shoot turret1 20 20 1
sensor sx turret1 @shootX
sensor sy turret1 @shootY
sensor sh turret1 @shooting
print sx
end
probes.why: control shoot takes TILE coordinates (Turret.java:381-386 World.unconv(p1), World.unconv(p2)) and @shootX/@shootY read them back converted; the third operand is only a non-zero flag

probes.code:
ubind @flare
wait 1.6
ucontrol itemTake container1 @copper 10
wait 0.1
sensor n @unit @totalItems
print n
end
probes.why: flare (itemCapacity 10) and a container 6 tiles away: item transfer runs on a 90-tick (1.5 s) cooldown (LogicAI.java:16 transferDelay, LExecutor.java:98 timeoutDone), and the sim's Time.time starts near zero, so the first take needs a 1.6 s wait; then the reach is Vars.java:125 logicItemTransferRange 45 world + block.size*4 -- 53 world = 6.625 tiles, so this is inside

probes.code:
ubind @flare
wait 1.6
ucontrol itemTake container1 @copper 10
wait 0.1
sensor n @unit @totalItems
print n
end
probes.why: flare (itemCapacity 10) and a container 8 tiles away: item transfer runs on a 90-tick (1.5 s) cooldown (LogicAI.java:16 transferDelay, LExecutor.java:98 timeoutDone), and the sim's Time.time starts near zero, so the first take needs a 1.6 s wait; then the reach is Vars.java:125 logicItemTransferRange 45 world + block.size*4 -- past 6.625 tiles the take silently does nothing
